simulator.strands_of_fate.quoted_text: At the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, roll 6D6 and set those dice aside; this is your pool of Fate dice. Each time an AELDARI model from your army is the source of an attack, or a unit from your army is the target of an attack, or a unit from your army is making an Advance, Charge, or Battle-shock roll, before making any of those rolls, you can select a Fate dice from your pool to use as the substitute for that roll, even if such a roll would not normally be made. Then remove that Fate dice from your pool.
simulator.strands_of_fate.trigger: any d6 roll made by an AELDARI unit (hit, wound, save, charge, advance, Battle-shock) or by an opponent against an AELDARI unit; pool is rolled at start of battle round 1
simulator.strands_of_fate.effect: (approximation) Army.fate_dice is populated with 6D6 at battle start. Spent greedily by a heuristic that pops the lowest qualifying die in the pool to flip a fail->success on hit rolls (Aeldari attacker), save rolls (Aeldari target), charge rolls (Aeldari charger), and advance rolls (Aeldari mover). Per-unit spend gates — implemented via Army._unit_budget_used keyed by effect name, with key = squad_id (int) when >= 0 else profile name (str), reset each battle round — enforce the codex rule that each unit may make at most one substitution per roll type per round. AELDARI-STRANDS-V1: advance-roll spending gated to one spend per codex unit per round (effect key 'fate_advance'). FATE-CHARGE-V1: charge-roll spending gated to one spend per codex unit per round (effect key 'fate_charge'), fixing a squad multi-spend bug where every model in a squad independently entered the substitution and could drain one Fate die each for a single shared charge roll. Pool depletes; once empty, no further substitutions. The simulator's spend AI is conservative — it never spends a Fate die on a roll that would still fail, and it does not yet model defensive substitution of the opponent's hit/wound dice or Battle-shock substitution.
